failures.detail: hw-n11 ↔ hw-p2-c linked by the deterministic rules (score 0.9: same street and unit 410 in 33166); rule-certain links never reach the model. hw-n11 ↔ hw-p2-a linked by the deterministic rules (score 0.9: same street and unit 410 in 33166); rule-certain links never reach the model.
failures.analysis: Freight forwarders give every customer the same street and suite and tell them apart by a box/PMB number. Our normaliser keeps only the first unit token ('Ste 410') and drops the box (88213 vs 90577), so a legitimate international fan who uses the same Miami forwarder as a reseller is linked to the reseller with certainty (score 0.9), and rule-certain links never reach the model. In production this is still only a suggestion that the seller must confirm and the fan can appeal, but it is the error we care about most. Planned fix: parse PMB/Box/'#suite-box' as a sub-unit and make 'same suite, different box' uncertain (reviewed by the model) instead of certain. Deliberately not applied before publishing, so the held-out number stays blind.

failures.analysis: Same root cause as the false merge, seen from the other side: '#410-88213' and 'STE 410-88213' normalise to one unit '41088213' instead of suite 410 + box 88213, and '8240 NW 52 Ter' vs '52nd Ter' scores 0.875 on street similarity, just under our 0.88 threshold, so Sofia Mendes's account is never flagged. The model linked 3 of the 4 accounts in runs 2 and 3; in run 1 it returned an empty answer for this group (token budget, see ho-net3), which left only the 2 rule-certain links.

failures.detail: Run 1: 4 true pairs missed: 4 were in a group the model never answered (empty or truncated answer on both attempts), so they stayed unmerged.
failures.analysis: Not a judgement error. In all 3 runs MiMo returned an empty answer, twice, for this group of 5. MiMo V2.6 Pro is a reasoning model and its reasoning tokens count against max_tokens: with our 2,000-token cap it spent the whole budget thinking (reproduced with a direct call: finish_reason 'length', 1,999 reasoning tokens, no content; with 8,000 it answers). Paylet failed safe: the pairs stayed unmerged and the run was flagged as degraded. The rules alone linked 4 of the 5 accounts; the fifth ('Bldg 1, No. 7B', where the normaliser takes 'Bldg 1' as the unit) needed the model. Fix: the adjudication budget is now 6,000 tokens (see the after-fix section).

failures.detail: Run 1: 4 true pairs missed: 4 were never flagged by the rules (score below the review threshold), so the model never saw them.
failures.analysis: The red-team wrote 'Ste 4B' as 'STE4B' (no space) and misspelled Boulevard as 'Bvld'. Our unit pattern needs a word boundary after 'STE', so the unit becomes 'STE4B', and street similarity drops to 0.875, just under 0.88: that account is never flagged and the model never sees it. The other 4 accounts of this operation were linked in every run (the model read 'Bldg 1, Ste 4-B' and 'No. 4-B' correctly from what was typed), so the operation gets 2 allocations instead of 1, not 5. Planned fix: accept glued unit tokens ('STE4B', 'APT2') and spell-check street suffixes before comparing.

notes: Dev set: 123 true pairs; only 52 fuzzy pairs (of 14196) go to the model, everything else is decided by deterministic rules.

Held-out set (blind): generated after the rules and prompt were frozen (other seed, other red-team template, hand-written neighbours, namesakes and forwarder customers). 70 true pairs, 34 fuzzy pairs sent to the model.
Paylet numbers are the mean of 3 independent model runs (± sample standard deviation); the worst run is published too.
Every model answer is recorded in evals/cassette.json: `pnpm evals --replay` reproduces these numbers offline, without a key.
In production nothing is auto-merged: these suggestions go to the seller, and fans can appeal.
